Introduction
The following document is the user guide of the REST API for Customer360. It includes the
model definition as well as the available operations.
API Overview and Objectives
The Customer360 API provides a comprehensive, unified view of customer information by
aggregating data from multiple sources into a single, read-only resource. This API serves
the following key objectives:
•
Holistic
Customer
View
:
Combines
customer
information
from
various
domains
(accounts,
products,
bills,
tickets,
appointments,
agreements,
etc.)
into
a
single
consolidated resource
•
Operational Efficiency
: Enables applications to retrieve complete customer context in
a single API call, reducing the need for multiple API requests across different systems
•
Enhanced Customer Experience
: Supports customer-facing applications (such as call
centers, self-service portals, and mobile apps) with comprehensive customer data for
better service delivery
•
Read-Only Access
: Provides a safe, non-intrusive way to access aggregated customer
data without modifying underlying systems
Main Concepts and Resources
The Customer360 API manages the following main resource:
•
Customer360
◦
Customer360 is a read-only resource that aggregates comprehensive information
about a customer from multiple domains
◦
The unique identifier of the Customer360 resource equals the customer identifier in
the Customer Management API
◦
Main components include:
▪
Customer basic information (name, status, contact details, related parties)
▪
Accounts (billing accounts, settlement accounts)
▪
Agreements (commercial agreements, service level agreements)
▪
Appointments (scheduled interventions, service visits)
▪
Customer bills (invoices, payment status)
Customer360 User Guide

Page 1
▪
Loyalty accounts (loyalty points, rewards balance)
▪
Party interactions (customer service interactions, store visits)
▪
Payment methods (credit cards, bank accounts)
▪
Products (subscribed products and services)
▪
Product orders (order history, order status)
▪
Usage records (product usage and consumption patterns)
▪
Quotes (customer quotes, pricing information)
▪
Service problems (service issues, problem tracking)
▪
Trouble tickets (open issues, service requests)
Important
Note
on
Value
Objects:
All
Value
Object
(VO)
entities
defined
within
the
Customer360
domain
represent
subsets
of
their
corresponding
source
entities.
Consequently, the attributes declared within each VO schema object constitute a subset
of the attribute definitions present in their respective originating schema objects.
The Customer360 API performs the following operations:
•
Retrieval of complete customer 360-degree view
•
List/query operations with filtering capabilities
•
Event notifications for customer data changes
API Dependencies
This API aggregates information from multiple TM Forum APIs and assumes that detailed
information can be obtained by accessing the following APIs:
•
TMF629 Customer Management API
: For detailed customer information
•
TMF666 Account Management API
: For account details and financial information
•
TMF651 Agreement Management API
: For agreement and contract information
•
TMF646 Appointment API
: For appointment scheduling information
•
TMF678 Customer Bill Management API
: For billing and invoice details
•
TMF658 Loyalty Management API
: For loyalty account and rewards information
•
TMF683 Party Interaction API
: For customer interaction history
•
TMF670 Payment Method API
: For payment method information
•
TMF637 Product Inventory API
: For product and service subscription details

Use Case 1: Call Center Customer Service Representative
Dashboard
Business Context
In
a
telecommunications
service
provider
environment,
call
center
representatives
need
immediate
access
to
comprehensive
customer
information
to
provide
efficient
and
personalized service. When a customer calls with a question or issue, the representative
must quickly understand the customer’s complete context including their products, billing
status, open tickets, scheduled appointments, and interaction history.
Actors
•
Call Center Representative (primary actor)
•
Customer (initiating actor)
•
Customer360 API (supporting system)
•
Call Center Application (supporting system)
Preconditions
•
Customer is identified and authenticated (customer ID: 1140)
•
Call center representative has access to the customer service application
•
Customer360 data has been aggregated from source systems
Main Flow
1.
Customer
"Moon
Football
Club"
(ID:
1140)
calls
the
call
center
regarding
their
internet
service
2.
Call
center
representative
enters
or
receives
the
customer
identifier
(1140)
in
the
system
3.
The call center application invokes:
GET /customer360/1140
4.
The Customer360 API returns a comprehensive customer profile containing:
◦
Customer
Information
:
Name
"Moon
Football
Club",
status
"Approved",
contact

Use Case 2: Self-Service Customer Portal
Business Context
Customers access a self-service web portal to view their complete profile, manage their
services,
and
track
their
interactions
with
the
service
provider.
The
portal
uses
the
Customer360 API to present a unified dashboard.
Main Flow

Page 6
1.
Customer logs into the self-service portal
2.
Portal application retrieves Customer360 data for the authenticated customer
3.
Dashboard displays:
◦
Account summary with current status and balance
◦
Active products and services
◦
Recent bills and payment history
◦
Loyalty points and rewards
◦
Scheduled appointments
◦

4.
Customer can navigate to detailed management APIs for specific actions (e.g., pay bill,

Benefits
•
Single API call reduces page load time
•
Consistent customer experience across channels
•
Real-time aggregated view of customer data
Use Case 3: Proactive Customer Retention
Business Context
A retention team uses analytics dashboards powered by Customer360 API to identify at-
risk customers and take proactive measures.
Main Flow
1.
Retention
application
queries
Customer360
API
with
filters:
GET
/customer360?customer.status=Active&fields=customer,products,custome
rBill,troubleTicket
2.
Application analyzes patterns:
◦
Multiple open trouble tickets
◦
Suspended or cancelled products
◦
Overdue bills
◦
Reduced usage patterns
3.
Retention team receives alerts for at-risk customers
Customer360 User Guide

4.
Team retrieves complete Customer360 view for each at-risk customer
5.

◦

◦
Interaction history
Benefits
•
Early identification of churn risk
•
Data-driven retention strategies
•
Improved customer lifetime value

Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections
occurs
when
entities
inherit
from
base
entities.
In
the
Customer360
API
context,
polymorphism
is
demonstrated
through
contact
medium
types
and
reference
entities.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).
Meta-Attributes for Polymorphism
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example,
within
the
Customer360
resource,
the
contactMedium
collection
can
contain
different types of contact mediums:
•
PhoneContactMedium
- for phone contact information
•
GeographicAddressContactMedium
- for physical address information
•
EmailContactMedium
- for email contact information
All
these
types
inherit
from
the
base
ContactMedium
entity.
The
@type
attribute
indicates
which
specific
type
is
being
used.
All
resources
and
sub-resources
of
this
API
have @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.
Example from Customer360 API:
In
the
Customer360
resource,
the
customer’s
contactMedium
array
demonstrates
polymorphism:
"contactMedium": [
  {
 
"@type": "PhoneContactMedium",
 
"@baseType": "ContactMedium",
 
"@schemaLocation": "/schema-registry/schema/PhoneContactMedium",
 
"id": "2256789876",
 
"preferred": true,
 
"contactType": "homePhone",
 
"phoneNumber": "01 09 75 83 51"
  },
  {
 
"@type": "GeographicAddressContactMedium",
 
"@baseType": "ContactMedium",
 
"@schemaLocation": "/schema-registry/schema/GeographicAddressContactMedium",
Customer360 User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 9
 
"id": "12345",
 
"preferred": false,
 
"contactType": "homeAddress",
 
"city": "Paris",
 
"country": "France",
 
"postCode": "75014",
 
"street1": "15 Rue des Canards"
  }
]
The
@referredType
can
be
used
within
reference
entities
(like
for
instance
a
PartyRef
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Notice
that
in
reference
entities
the
@type,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type
of
the
reference
itself,
such as PartyRef or OrganizationRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However
since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference
objects.
Example from Customer360 API:
In
the
Customer360
resource,
the
engagedParty
reference
demonstrates
the
use
of
@referredType:
"engagedParty": {
  "@type": "PartyRef",
  "href": "https://host:port/tmf-api/partyManagement/v4/organization/500",
  "id": "500",
  "name": "Happy Travellers",
  "@referredType": "Organization"
}
Here,
@type
indicates
this
is
a
PartyRef
(the
reference
type),
while
@referredType
indicates the actual referred entity is an Organization. The referred entity could also be an
Individual, depending on the customer type.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.
Example from Customer360 API:
{
  "@type": "Customer360",
  "@schemaLocation": "/schema-registry/schema/Customer360.yaml",
  "href": "https://host:port/tmf-api/customer360/v5/customer360/1140",
  "id": "1140"
}
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
of
class
of
a
given
Customer360 User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 10
resource that has been extended.
Example from Customer360 API:
In the contactMedium examples above, the @baseType attribute explicitly indicates that
both
PhoneContactMedium
and
GeographicAddressContactMedium
inherit
from
the
ContactMedium base type.
Additional Polymorphism Examples in Customer360
The Customer360 API also demonstrates polymorphism in other areas:
•
Value
Objects
:
Different
types
of
value
objects
(e.g.,
Customer360AccountVO,
Customer360ProductVO,
Customer360CustomerBillVO)
that
represent
aggregated
views of different domain entities
•
Related
Party
References
:
The
relatedParty
collection
can
contain
references
to
different party types (Organization, Individual) with appropriate @referredType values
•
Payment
Methods
:
Different
payment
method
types
(CreditCard,
BankAccount,
DigitalWallet)
can
be
represented
in
the
paymentMethod
collection
with
appropriate
@type discrimination

Customer360 User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 34
An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different
from
the
current
system,
for
example
a
ProductOrder
handed
off
from
a
commerce
platform
into
an
order
handling
system.
The
structure
identifies
the
system
itself,
the
nature
of
the
entity
within
the
system
(e.g.
class
name)
and
the
unique
ID
of
the
entity
within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity,
e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this
case
the
consumer
is
expected
to
sequence
the
IDs
in
the
array
in
reverse
order
of
provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.
externalIdentifierType
A String. Type of the identification, typically would be the
type of the entity within the external system.
id
A String [1]. Identification of the entity within the external
system.
owner
A String. Name of the external system that owns the
entity.

MultiLineString and Polygon (countries, provinces, tracts of land). Use the @type attribute
to specify which of these is being specified by the geometry attribute.

A bbox. A bounding box array that contains the geometry.
The axes order follows the axes order of the geometry.

CalendarPeriod sub-resource fields
The CalendarPeriod schema represents a period of time within a calendar, defining various
attributes such as the applicable day, timezone, hour period, and status. It is designed to
capture information about the availability or status of a calendar period, which can be used
in scheduling, booking, or resource allocation applications.
day
A DayOfWeekType. Possible values for the days of the
week. ENUMERATED with values:
* mon
* tue
* wed
* thu
* fri
* sat
* sun
* weekdays
* weekend
hourPeriod
A HourPeriod [0..*]. Start and end time range in 24-hour
HH:mm format.
status
A String [1]. Indication of the availability of the calendar
period (e.g.: available, booked, etc.).

calendar information in ISO 8601 timezone: either 'Z' for

building cluster, or a floor of a multistory building.

A String. Allows for buildings that have well-known names.

A String. Unique Identifier of the subAddress.

A String. Used where a level type may be repeated e.g.

meaningful identification.
privateStreetName
A String. Private streets internal to a property (e.g. a

by the land title office.

street.

private street.

WHARF.

A String. Free form text describing the Service Problem.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
originatingSystem
A String. Indicates where the problem was generated.
Customer360 User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 114
priority
An Integer. An indication varying from 1 (highest) to 10
(lowest) of how important it is for the service provider to
correct the Service Problem.
reason
A String. Reason, if known, for the service problem that will
assist the Service Provider in understanding the
underlying cause or contributing factors, enabling more
accurate diagnosis and resolution. This can be set to
Unknown, otherwise.
status
A String. The current status of the service problem.
Possible values are Submitted, Rejected, Acknowledged, In
Progress [Held, Pending], Resolved, Closed, and Cancelled.
@baseType
A String. When sub-classing, this defines the super-class.

additional attributes and relationships.
@type
A String [1]. When sub-classing, this defines the sub-class
Extensible name.
Customer360TroubleTicketVO sub-resource fields
TroubleTicket value object to contain the important information about the trouble tickets
for a customer.
creationDate
A DateTime. The date on which the trouble ticket was
created.
description
A String. Description of the trouble or issue.
expectedResolutionDate
A DateTime. The expected resolution date determined by
the trouble ticket system.
externalIdentifier
A String. Additional identifier coming from an external
system.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
lastUpdate
A DateTime. The date and time that the trouble ticked was
last updated.
name
A String. Name of the trouble ticket, typically a short
description provided by the user that create the ticket.
Customer360 User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 115
priority
A String. The priority of the trouble ticket and how quickly
the issue should be resolved. Example: Critical, High,
Medium, Low. The value is set by the ticket management
system considering the severity, ticket type etc...
requestedResolutionDate
A DateTime. The resolution date requested by the user.
severity
A String. The severity of the issue. Indicate the implication
of the issue on the expected functionality e.g. of a system,
application, service etc.. Severity values can be for
example : Critical, Major, Minor.
status
A TroubleTicketStatusType. Possible values for the status
of the trouble ticket. ENUMERATED with values:
* acknowledged
* rejected
* pending
* held
* inProgress
* cancelled
* closed
* resolved
statusChangeDate
A DateTime. The date and time the status changed.
statusChangeReason
A String. The reason for changing the status.
ticketType
A String. Represent a business type of the trouble ticket e.
g. incident, complain, request.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
Customer360 User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 148
{
 
"id":"42",
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com",
 
"query":""
}
Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.
Request
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
Response
204
Publish Event to listener
POST /client/listener
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.
Provides
to
a
registered
listener
the
description
of
the
event
that
was
raised.
The
/client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.
Customer360 User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 149
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE”
should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification
resources
Models
section)
and
EVENT
BODY
refers
to
the
data
structure
of
the
given
notification type.
Request
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
 
"event": {
 
EVENT BODY
 
},
 
"eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
Response
201
For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST
Design Guidelines.
